subject: spanish
title: Stamp 2: Monarchy and Cortes Generales
welcome_lead: Stamp Spain's constitutional monarchy and bicameral parliament.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on King Felipe VI, the Cortes, and the major parties.

concepts.def: King of Spain since June 2014 after his father Juan Carlos I abdicated.
Spain's bicameral parliament: Congreso de los Diputados + Senado.
Lower house with 350 deputies elected by proportional representation.
Upper house, mostly elected, with limited revising powers.
Partido Socialista Obrero Espanol; centre-left, governing party under Pedro Sanchez.
Partido Popular; centre-right successor of Alianza Popular.

walkthroughs.body_html: The monarch is head of state with mainly symbolic and arbitral functions. Felipe VI proposes a candidate for prime minister after general elections; the Congreso then votes on investiture.
Congreso seats are distributed by the D'Hondt method in 52 provincial constituencies, favouring larger parties and regionalist forces concentrated in particular provinces.
Traditional bipartidismo (PSOE vs PP) gave way after 2014-15 to multi-party politics including Podemos (left), Ciudadanos (now reduced), Vox (far right), and Sumar.
